listing.name: Street Fighter II: Hyper Fighting (CPS-2 Recomp)
listing.summary: Play Street Fighter II: Hyper Fighting in CPS-2 Recomp using your own matching arcade files.

restrictions.explanation: This CPS-2 Recomp test build needs an existing copy. Choose a full collection release for a new setup.

steps.title: Get the matching arcade files
steps.instruction: Use your own Street Fighter II': Hyper Fighting (World 921209) arcade ROM set (`sf2hf`).

steps.title: Set up the game in the collection
steps.instruction: Extract the complete package for your system. Open CPS-2 Recomp and select the ROM folder on its Games page. Pick the game and press Play.

steps.title: Start the prepared game again
steps.instruction: Choose Play in CPS-2 Recomp. On desktop, a frontend can call the collection launcher with two arguments, `--play` and `sf2hf`. Open the launcher without arguments to change the ROM folder or settings.

warnings: This upstream package is a prerelease. Portcove has package evidence for this version. Individual gameplay and save restoration are unverified.

references.title: Linux ARM64 and Android
references.instruction: For Linux ARM64, use CPS2Recomp-linux-arm64.tar.gz and run cps2recomp-launcher. On an ARM64 device running Android 9 or later, install CPS2Recomp-android.apk and use Games → Add ROM sets. Get both packages and their checksums from the upstream release page.

references.title: Find saves and update the collection
references.instruction: Use Your files → Show in the launcher to find the actual launcher and game folders. With portable.txt beside the launcher or Mac app, the collection uses user/ there. Keep your settings, saves and the working package before replacing it. The shared launcher offers updates. Leave its files together and manage them outside Portcove.

source_editions.title: Street Fighter II: Hyper Fighting (CPS-1, World 921209, sf2hf)

original_game_review.reason: Keep separately named historical Street Fighter II arcade releases distinct: World Warrior, Champion Edition, Hyper Fighting, Super, Super Turbo and Anniversary Edition change playable rosters, combat rules or cross-version character selection. Regions/revisions within each game do not create additional identities; shared translated program lineage does not collapse these releases.
